newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO detains six Arabs for land sales to Jews.
newsitem.headline: PLO detains six Arabs for land sales to Jews.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority, under fire from Washington over its intention to punish by death people who sell land to Jews, said on Thursday it had detained six Arabs on suspicion of violating the land sale ban.
"There are six Palestinian residents in custody on suspicion of selling lands," Attorney General Khaled al-Kidra told Reuters.
He said if convicted, the six could face the death penalty according to a Jordanian law inherited by the authority.

"We have not brought anyone to trial yet and we have not prepared charge sheets either. The investigation is under way and once it is over we will implement the law and the punishment may reach the death sentence," Kidra said.

Kidra gave no details about the arrests. But a Palestinian newspaper, al-Hayat al-Jadida, quoted him as saying that four of the suspects are from the West Bank town of Hebron and two from smaller nearby villages.
The United States on Wednesday strongly criticised Palestinian President Yasser Arafat after an Israeli newspaper quoted him as backing the decision to enforce the death penalty.

"The United States condemns any law or any decree that would threaten death against any Palestinian for selling land to Israelis or Jews," U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said. "That's wrong. It's contrary to what must prevail in the Middle East, which is peace."
A senior Arafat aide on Thursday rejected the U.S. criticism, saying Washington was misinformed.
"I hope that they (the U.S.) would not rush to judgments on sensitive issues that the Palestinian Authority is dealing with wisely," aide Ahmed Abdel-Rahman told Reuters.
"There is wrong information emanating from the Israeli side and the Palestinian side is willing to explain its position at all levels to American officials," he said.

The Palestinian Authority, concerned over an Israeli government drive to expand Jewish settlements in the West Bank, recently banned land sales to Jews and its justice minister said a Jordanian law which provides for the death penalty would be applied against offenders.
Jordan took control of the West Bank in the 1948 Middle East war. Israel has occupied it since the 1967 war.

Israel has linked the ban on land sales with the recent killings of two Palestinian land dealers found dead in the West Bank. The authority, which says the law is applied by the courts and not vigilantes, has denied any involvement in the killings.
Israel said on Wednesday it would complain to the U.N. commission on human rights over the land sale ban and death penalty, saying they "reeked of anti-Semitism".
Abdel-Rahman said the Palestinian Authority would provide fair and public hearings against anyone charged with land sales.

Palestinians say the purchase of land by Jews and Israeli settlement building in Jerusalem, the rest of the West Bank, and Gaza pre-empts final peace talks on the fate of the areas where they hope someday to establish an independent state.
